sofia-sec: Heads-up: rolling out a change to privileged role session policies today. Starting next week we will enforce a maximum session duration of 1 hour for all `admin/*` and `ops/*` roles and require MFA for assume-role flows. This is a preventive hardening step after the privilege audit.

jamal-iam: Quick background: we found ~14 roles with no session-duration limit and several automation runs that relied on long-lived assume-role tokens. Risk: stolen tokens could be used for lateral movement for longer than necessary.

kai-sre: Affects internal IAM only, not customer-facing API keys. Dedicated control planes that use our org IAM for operator accounts will be impacted if they rely on long sessions.

sofia-sec: Immediate actions: 1) audit and list owners of roles without max session (we have a query), 2) set a temporary enforcement flag org-wide for non-service accounts (start now, 48h leniency for human owners), 3) plan removal of the leniency and full enforcement in 7 days.

bot-deploy: Ticket created: SEC-11234. Audit query results uploaded: https://infra.redwood-internal/iam/audit/SEC-11234 (internal).

jamal-iam: Commands to set policy (redwood-cli):

jamal-iam: ```bash
# set max session to 3600s for a role
redwood-cli iam update-role --role admin-ops --max-session-duration 3600
# require MFA for assume-role
redwood-cli iam update-role --role admin-ops --require-mfa true
```

ben-platform: For Dedicated customers that map to `platform-admin` role in our control plane, we need to coordinate with CS. Will the change break automation?

sofia-sec: Service accounts with automated workflows will be exempt from the 48h human leniency but must migrate to short-lived OIDC tokens or use role chaining with a controlled token exchange. We'll publish migration snippets.

alia-cs: I'll start outreach to teams that own `platform-*` roles and offer assisted migration. Add a clear opt-out form for critical rollback requests.

nora-legal: For compliance, include an exception review process for roles that cannot be migrated in time (FedRAMP clients may need extra steps). Keep a record of exception approvals.

jamal-iam: Migration examples (GitHub Actions):

jamal-iam: ```yaml
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Exchange OIDC for short lived role credentials
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(curl -fsS "https://oauth.redwood-internal/token?aud=ci&sa=${{secrets.SA_NAME}}")
          redwood-cli sts assume-role --role platform-deploy --token "$TOKEN" --duration 3600 > creds.json
      - name: Use creds
        run: ./deploy.sh --creds creds.json
```

kai-sre: We'll also add detection: alert if a role session lasts >1h or unusual role chaining occurs. SRE will tune alerts to reduce noise during rollout.

sofia-sec: Timeline: NOW - run audit and notify owners; T+48h - auto-set max-session on non-service roles but allow human owners to request exceptions; T+7 days - full enforcement, revoke outstanding long sessions older than 1h.

ben-platform: What's the revocation command?

jamal-iam: To expire sessions we will call the session manager revoke API: `redwood-cli sts revoke-sessions --role <role-name> --older-than 3600`

alia-cs: I'll prepare messaging for internal teams and a short customer note for Dedicated tenants that may be affected.

nora-legal: Ensure exception requests include business justification and mitigation steps. Legal to review templates.

bot-deploy: SEC-11234 updated: enforcement flag set to `audit-only=true` for 48h. Playbook: https://wiki.redwood-internal/runbooks/privileged-session-hardening.

sofia-sec: Please prioritize notifying any teams that have scheduled automation relying on >1h sessions (CI, deploy scripts, monitoring bridges). Tag me if you need expedited exception review.

kai-sre: We'll monitor auth logs for unexpected drops and be ready to revert to `audit-only` for specific tenants if a critical outage appears.

sofia-sec: Thanks all. After enforcement we'll run a short post-change review and publish findings. :lock:
